## Task
TASK.md asked for the cause and a minimal source fix for "Combine fast delete queries" (Django ticket #30856) — cascade deletions issuing one `DELETE ... WHERE fk IN (...)` per foreign key instead of one combined query per table. No test changes, no commit.

## Cause
In `django/db/models/deletion.py`, `Collector.collect()` decided fast-delete eligibility **per relation** (`can_fast_delete(sub_objs, from_field=field)` on each fetched queryset) and appended one queryset to `self.fast_deletes` per FK. A model with N FKs to the same table (e.g. `Entry.created_by`/`updated_by`, `Person.friends` self-M2M) therefore produced N separate DELETE roundtrips.

## Fix (working tree, uncommitted)
Adapted from the upstream fix found in this clone's history (`26c66f4519`, "Fixed #30856 -- Combined fast-delete queries by model during cascade deletion"), fitted to this checkout's older structure (its `if collect_related:` block, non-`defaultdict` data structures):

- `django/db/models/deletion.py`
  - `can_fast_delete` now takes the **model** (`objs._meta.model`) so eligibility is decided before any query.
